description_full: CorMedix Inc., a biopharmaceutical company, focuses on developing and commercializing therapeutic products for life-threatening diseases and conditions in the United States. Its lead product candidate is DefenCath, an antimicrobial catheter lock solution to reduce the incidence of catheter-related bloodstream infections in adult patients with kidney failure. CorMedix Inc. was formerly known as Picton Holding Company, Inc. and changed its name to CorMedix, Inc. in January 2007. The company was incorporated in 2006 and is based in Parsippany, New Jersey.
ceo_bio: Mr. Joseph  Todisco MBA | CEO & Chairman of the Board of Directors | Age 49 | Compensation: $1.6M (FY2025)
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 191 people. Revenue per employee of $1.6M ranks in the top quartile among Healthcare peers, improving at 171%/yr — growing workforce leverage. Each employee generates $905K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $72K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 1× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags moderate compensation governance risk (6/10).
financial_summary: CorMedix Inc. is a small-cap healthcare business with a $415M market cap on $312M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +1077% over the past three years and +108% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +22335.9pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.

Returns on capital run at 20% against a 10% cost of capital — a 10-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, and 11% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $173M in free cash flow — roughly 55 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.07× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 54× is fortress-like.

Net dilution runs at 1.9% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insiders hold 7.6% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 5.5× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
